questions.knowledge_point: Computing Variance Using the Definition Given a Probability Mass Function
questions.problem:
Let $X$ be the outcome of rolling an unfair tetrahedral  die that follows the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below. What is $\text{Var}[X]?$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ |
questions.worked_solution:
The variance of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{Var}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

First, we need to compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4) \\  & =1(\frac{3}{8})+2(\frac{3}{8})+3(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=2$ into the variance formula, we get

$$
\text{Var}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}(x-2)^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

Now, we compute the variance as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =(1-2)^{2}\cdot f(1)+(2-2)^{2}\cdot f(2)+(3-2)^{2}\cdot f(3)+(4-2)^{2}\cdot f(4) \\  & =f(1)+0+f(3)+4\cdot f(4) \\  & =(\frac{3}{8})+0+(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

The variance of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{Var}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ Here, there are $6$ possible outcomes ($-3,-1,2,3,5,12$) and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

| $x$ | $-3$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $5$ | $12$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ |

Now, we need to compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =(-3)\cdot f(-3)+(-1)\cdot f(-1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+5\cdot f(5)+12\cdot f(12) \\  & =(-3)(\frac{1}{6})+(-1)(\frac{1}{6})+2(\frac{1}{6})+3(\frac{1}{6})+5(\frac{1}{6})+12(\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=3$ into the variance formula, we get

$$
\text{Var}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}(x-3)^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

Now, we compute the variance as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =(-3-3)^{2}\cdot f(-3)+(-1-3)^{2}\cdot f(-1)+(2-3)^{2}\cdot f(2)+(3-3)^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & +(5-3)^{2}\cdot f(5)+(12-3)^{2}\cdot f(12) \\  & =36\cdot f(-3)+16\cdot f(-1)+1\cdot f(2)+0\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(5)+81\cdot f(12) \\  & =36(\frac{1}{6})+16(\frac{1}{6})+1(\frac{1}{6})+0+4(\frac{1}{6})+81(\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =23\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =(-2)\cdot f(-2)+(-1)\cdot f(-1)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3) \\  & =(-2)(\frac{1}{5})+(-1)(\frac{1}{5})+1(\frac{1}{5})+2(\frac{1}{5})+3(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & =(-2)^{2}\cdot f(-2)+(-1)^{2}\cdot f(-1)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & =4(\frac{1}{5})+1(\frac{1}{5})+1(\frac{1}{5})+4(\frac{1}{5})+9(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{19}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{19}{5}-{(\frac{3}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{19}{5}-\frac{9}{25} \\  & =\frac{95}{25}-\frac{9}{25} \\  & =\frac{86}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{86}{25}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{86}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{6})+2(\frac{1}{3})+3(\frac{1}{6})+4(\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{6})+4(\frac{1}{3})+9(\frac{1}{6})+16(\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{25}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{25}{3}-{(\frac{8}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{25}{3}-\frac{64}{9} \\  & =\frac{11}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{11}{9}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{11}}{3}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Several egg cartons were checked for cracked eggs. The number of cracked eggs in each carton was recorded below. Based on this data, if the random variable $N$ represents the number of cracked eggs in a randomly selected carton, what is $\text{SD}[N]?$

| Number of Cartons | $3$ | $8$ | $5$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cracked Eggs | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
questions.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $N$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[N]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[N]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[N]=\text{E}[{N}^{2}]-\text{E}[N]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(n).$ To do this, we divide each frequency by the total, which is $3+8+5+4=20.$ We get the following result:

| $f(n)$ | $\frac{3}{20}$ | $\frac{2}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $n$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |

Now, we compute $\text{E}[N]$ by summing up the products of each value of $N$ and its associated probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[N] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3) \\  & =0+(\frac{2}{5})+2(\frac{1}{4})+3(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[{N}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${N}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{N}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & =0+(\frac{2}{5})+4(\frac{1}{4})+9(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{16}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[N] & =\text{E}[{N}^{2}]-\text{E}[N]^{2} \\  & =\frac{16}{5}-{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{16}{5}-\frac{9}{4} \\  & =\frac{19}{20}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[N] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[N]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{19}{20}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{19}}{2\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{95}}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ Here, there are $7$ possible outcomes ($1,2,3,4,5,6,7$) and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ |

Next, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4)+5\cdot f(5)+6\cdot f(6)+7\cdot f(7) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{7})+2(\frac{1}{7})+3(\frac{1}{7})+4(\frac{1}{7})+5(\frac{1}{7})+6(\frac{1}{7})+7(\frac{1}{7}) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4)+{5}^{2}\cdot f(5)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6)+{7}^{2}\cdot f(7) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{7})+4(\frac{1}{7})+9(\frac{1}{7})+16(\frac{1}{7})+25(\frac{1}{7})+36(\frac{1}{7})+49(\frac{1}{7}) \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =20-{(4)}^{2} \\  & =20-16 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Let $X$ be the number obtained by a spinner with four sections labeled $1, 2, 3, 4.$ The probability mass function $f(x)$ of $X$ is shown in the table below. What is $\textrm{Var}[X]?$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ | $\dfrac{1}{4}$ | $\dfrac{1}{3}$ | $\dfrac{1}{4}$ |
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The variance of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} (x - \textrm E[X])^2 \cdot f(x).
$$

First, we need to compute $\textrm E[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{6})+2(\frac{1}{4})+3(\frac{1}{3})+4(\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\textrm E[X]=\dfrac{8}{3}$ into the variance formula, we get

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} \left(x - \dfrac{8}{3} \right)^2 \cdot f(x).
$$

Now, we compute the variance as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & ={(1-\frac{8}{3})}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{(2-\frac{8}{3})}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{(3-\frac{8}{3})}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{(4-\frac{8}{3})}^{2}\cdot f(4) \\  & =\frac{25}{9}\cdot f(1)+\frac{4}{9}\cdot f(2)+\frac{1}{9}\cdot f(3)+\frac{16}{9}\cdot f(4) \\  & =\frac{25}{9}(\frac{1}{6})+\frac{4}{9}\cdot (\frac{1}{4})+\frac{1}{9}\cdot (\frac{1}{3})+\frac{16}{9}(\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{19}{18}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: A fair die with sides labeled with numbers $1$ through $6$ is thrown once. If $X$ is the outcome of the die, what is the variance of $X?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ Here, there are $6$ possible outcomes ($1,2,3,4,5,6$) and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ |

Next, we compute $\textrm E[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4)+5\cdot f(5)+6\cdot f(6) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{6})+2(\frac{1}{6})+3(\frac{1}{6})+4(\frac{1}{6})+5(\frac{1}{6})+6(\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $\textrm E[X^2].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X^2$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4)+{5}^{2}\cdot f(5)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{6})+4(\frac{1}{6})+9(\frac{1}{6})+16(\frac{1}{6})+25(\frac{1}{6})+36(\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =\frac{91}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{91}{6}-{(\frac{7}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{91}{6}-\frac{49}{4} \\  & =\frac{35}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$
